\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Cold- versus warm-cache query latency. Cold measurements evict every artifact from the page cache with \texttt{posix\_fadvise(DONTNEED)} before each query; the warm column re-runs the \emph{identical} query set, so the ratio is not confounded by query difficulty. The index is opened with \texttt{faiss.IO\_FLAG\_MMAP} and the manifest columns with \texttt{np.load(mmap\_mode=\textquotesingle r\textquotesingle)}, so engine construction costs only 2.2\,s and the remaining cost is paid as page faults during queries. The artifacts total 1119\,GB against 125\,GiB of RAM ($\approx8\times$), so the vector store cannot be fully cached at any point.}

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Exact brute-force baseline. One sequential pass computes cosine similarity against every indexed vector, casting \texttt{fp16} to \texttt{fp32} and L2-normalising per chunk, identical to the arithmetic the rerank performs. A single isolated query requires a whole pass; batching amortises one pass over all queries. \textbf{The baseline is not storage-bound and should not be read as a lower bound}: it sustained 114\,MB/s against a device measured at 213\,MB/s, because each chunk serialises read, conversion, normalisation and matrix multiply with no overlap. A pipelined implementation would reduce the speedups by roughly a factor of two.}
\label{tab:baseline}
\begin{tabular}{lr}

\midrule

Brute force, batched over 500 queries & 18.1\,s/query \\
Index, warm median (64, 500) & 118\,ms \\
